title: Grown-on-Membrane Assays
author: Isaac Núñez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jsfcnbn

steps.title: Co‑transform E. coli with plasmids
steps.instruction: Introduce the appropriate sender and receiver plasmids into E. coli cells. Sender plasmids encode HSL‑C6 or HSL‑C12 production together with mBeRFP reporter; receiver plasmids encode the corresponding quorum‑sensing response system with fluorescent reporters (sfGFP or CyOFP). Use the following plasmid combinations: Receiver Orange High (ROH) = pTet32LasR + pLas8O, Receiver Orange Low (ROL) = pTet32LasR + pLas33O, Receiver Green High (RGH) = 1LU2 + pLux34G, Receiver Green Low (RGL) = 1LU2 + pLux54G, Sender Lux High (SLuxH) = Std34BeRFP + pLac34LuxI, Sender Lux Low (SLuxL) = Std34BeRFP + pLac54LuxI, Sender Las High (SLasH) = Std34BeRFP + pLac34LasI, Sender Las Low (SLasL) = Std34BeRFP + pLac54LasI.

steps.title: Grow co‑transformed culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 1 mL of liquid LB medium containing the two appropriate antibiotics (e.g., kanamycin and carbenicillin) with the co‑transformed cells. Incubate at 37 °C with agitation until the culture reaches OD₆₀₀ = 0.03 (approximately 5 hours).

steps.title: Place sterile membrane on agar
steps.instruction: Working in a sterile environment, open the membrane package, grasp the membrane with sterilized tweezers, and lay it flat onto the surface of an LB‑agar plate.

steps.title: Spot cultures onto membrane
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, add 0.5 µL of each appropriate culture (from step 2) onto the designated wells of the membrane according to the experimental layout.

substeps.instruction: Pipette vertically to minimise lateral spread.
Avoid depositing culture into adjacent wells; leave at least one empty well between different strain spots (e.g., between senders and receivers).
Take care not to transfer culture to neighboring wells.

steps.title: Incubate membrane plate
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 37 °C. Fluorescent signals should become visible within the next 24 hours. Do not perform Las/HSL‑C12 experiments at room temperature, as the regulatory system does not function properly under those conditions.
